chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (revocable divorce), and if he wishes, he may take her back before she gives birth; but if she gives birth before he takes her back, then she is completely divorced from him, and he is considered one of the suitors (from the suitors).

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She became completely divorced from him (final divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorcing a pregnant woman and when does the divorce become final?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a pregnant woman’s divorce remains revocable (raj'i) until childbirth, distinguishing it from the standard three-month waiting period for non-pregnant women. It establishes that once she delivers, the marriage bond is fully severed (ba'in), requiring the husband to perform a new marriage contract (khitaab) to remarry her, a ruling rooted in the Quranic verse 65:4.
